Disrumpo.notes_markdown:
### Added

- **Version in the editor** — The plugin version is shown in the top bar, next to the Check for Updates button.

### Fixed

- **The plugin bundle reported version 0.8.0** — The bundle's `moduleinfo.json` (and, on macOS, the version Finder shows for the bundle) carried the shared build's version 0.8.0 instead of the plugin's own. It now matches the version shown in the editor. Hosts never used this value for anything audible; it matters for tools that list installed plugins.
- **The AUv3 version ran only on Apple Silicon** — In the macOS installer, the AUv3 app (`Disrumpo AUv3.app`) and the extension inside it were built for Apple Silicon only, while the VST3 and AU beside them were universal, so on an Intel Mac the AUv3 version did not load. Both are now universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), like the rest of the package.
- **The update check never worked on Linux** — The check could not fetch over https, so the update banner never appeared on Linux. It now fetches through the system's libcurl (`libcurl.so.4`, or `libcurl-gnutls.so.4`), loaded when the check runs; on a system without libcurl the check stays silent, as before.

Profundum.notes_markdown:
First release. Profundum is a mass bass instrument: one controllable bass voice, built around Mass, the Anchor, Spectral
Shift and Bass Morph, that moves from pure sub to a distorted speaker-grabber without losing its low-frequency centre. It
ships with the full sound-design surface as host parameters, a Main and an Advanced editor page, a live harmonic
spectrum, and a library of 60 factory presets.

### Added

- **Profundum is a plugin** — A registered VST3 instrument (`Profundum.vst3`, AU `aumu`/`Prfd`/`KrAt`, bundle `com.krateaudio.profundum`). Every note runs the whole mass-bass engine, and the engine's true-peak limiter is the last stage inside it.
- **One event input, one stereo output** — No audio input and no sidechain bus. The AU declares exactly one channel configuration, 0 in / 2 out.
- **Four global controls** — Output gain (attenuation only, -60 dB to 0 dB with silence at the bottom, smoothed, applied after the limiter so it can never push past the ceiling), voice mode (Mono or Poly), polyphony (1-8, four by default) and output ceiling (-12 to 0 dBTP, -1 by default). All four are saved with the project.
- **Four live Personality macros: Weight, Dark/Bright, Tight/Loose, Clean/Violent** — Each one moves the sound from the first release; the centre position (0.5) is neutral and changes nothing. All four are saved with the project.
- **Host tempo** — When the host reports a tempo, the engine's tempo-synced motion follows it; otherwise it runs at 120 BPM.
- **64 samples of reported latency** — Constant at every sample rate: the output limiter's look-ahead. The plugin reports its delay so the host can compensate.
- **Test suite `profundum_tests`** — Bus layout, parameter denormalisation, state round trip (hostile streams included), MIDI event ordering and overflow, lifecycle, editor lifecycle, wrapper transparency, parameter audibility, zero allocation on the audio thread, and a timed CPU case run on its own.
- **The full parameter surface: 95 parameters** — Every engine lever is a host parameter, in 100-ID bands: Mass and Morph Position beside the macros (104, 105), Core 200-210, Anchor 300-306, Drop / note behaviour / amp envelope 400-499 (Drop 400-403, note behaviour 410-417, amp envelope 420-426), Fold / Shape 500-501, Character 600-602, Mass dynamics 700-701, Stereo field 800-809, Motion 900-914 and Morph control 1000-1011 (Anchor Morph Mode, Edit Target, Morph Ramp Time, and the nine Morph Modulation controls 1003-1011).
- **Two endpoints, A and B, with an Edit Target** — The 60 sound parameters each hold an A and a B value and Morph Position moves between them. Edit Target chooses which endpoint you see and edit; switching it never changes the sound. Host automation of a sound parameter writes the endpoint selected by Edit Target when it plays back.
- **Copy and Compare** — Copy A to B / B to A, and Compare (A, A-B, B) to audition either endpoint without moving Morph Position. Both have buttons in the editor's morph section; Compare is never saved.
- **MIDI controllers** — Mod wheel and channel pressure push Mass up at every Morph Position without changing the saved sound; pitch bend with an adjustable range (Pitch Bend Range); a sustain pedal that holds released notes until it lifts.
- **Larger saved state** — Projects now save both endpoints, the note behaviour, the morph controls, the random seed and the morph's in-flight position (510 bytes, format version 2). Projects saved by the first scaffold build still load: their globals and macros are kept and every new parameter takes its default.
- **Release-aware tail** — The reported tail follows the longest amp release of the two endpoints, as lengthened or shortened by Tight/Loose, so a host never cuts a release short.
- **The editor: a Main page and an Advanced page** — Main holds the controls that shape a bass in seconds: voice mode, Weight, Dark/Bright and Clean/Violent, Mass, Bass Morph, Depth, Body and Edge, the Anchor waveform and level, Drop, Glide, Fold, the Motion source, Morph Behaviour and Edit Target. Advanced holds the rest in three tabs: Sections, Modulation and Settings. The window is a fixed 960 x 600 and every control has a tooltip.
- **A live harmonic spectrum** — The bars show the harmonics of the note you are playing, as you play it, with the Anchor shown on its own. When you play chords it shows the most recent note while that note sounds, then falls back to the one before. The display never changes the sound. In a host that offers neither VST3 data exchange nor a run loop (a bare test harness, for example) the spectrum stays empty.
- **Bass Morph in the editor** — Compare buttons (A, A-B, B) audition either endpoint without moving Morph Position, and Copy A to B / B to A copies one endpoint over the other. Each endpoint can be given a name (up to 31 bytes of text: 31 plain letters, fewer accented or non-Latin ones), saved with the project, and shows three words describing its shape, colour and force, such as Round, Warm, Clean. When Anchor Morph Mode is Hold and you edit B, the Anchor controls dim and read "Held at A": they still edit B, but the Anchor you hear stays at A.
- **Macro highlight and rings** — Hovering over or moving a Personality macro highlights the controls it acts on. A ring around each of those knobs shows how far the macro pushes it; the knob itself stays where you set it.
- **Zoom** — 100, 125, 150 or 200 %, chosen in the header or in the Settings tab. The zoom is kept for the session and is not saved with the project.
- **Endpoint names are saved** — The saved state grows to 626 bytes (format version 3) to hold the two names and, after them, the Morph Modulation block (its nine controls); each endpoint holds Stiffness and Phase. Projects saved by earlier builds still load, with the endpoints named A and B and Morph Modulation at its defaults (Source Off).
- **Morph Modulation** — Bass Morph can now move by itself. One global source, shared by every voice and outside both endpoints, moves the morph to clamp(Morph Position + Amount × source, 0, 1); Morph Position itself, and what presets and projects save, stay as you set them. Five sources: Off (the default), Envelope (Attack, Decay, Sustain; it restarts from 0 on every note-on the instrument accepts, in Mono and in Poly, and with no release it rests at Sustain until the next note), Cycle (six shapes, free rate or synced to the host tempo, free-running so a new note never makes the morph jump), Velocity (the latest note-on's velocity, held through note-offs) and Mod Wheel. With Mod Wheel as the source and a non-zero Amount, the wheel moves the morph and stops pushing Mass; at Amount 0 it keeps pushing Mass, so the wheel is never dead, and channel pressure pushes Mass with every source. COMPARE A or B plays the pure endpoint without the modulation, while the sources keep running so A·B resumes the gesture. The movement passes through Morph Ramp Time. Source and Amount sit in the Main page's Bass Morph band, all nine controls in the Advanced page's Modulation tab, and a marker on the Main page's Morph Position slider shows the morph position you actually hear. Presets that show it off: Poly Swell, Poly Spread, Poly Ignition and Rectified Floor (Envelope), Tidal Fold (Cycle), Struck Fold (Velocity) and Long Tail (Mod Wheel).
- **Stiffness and Phase** — Two core controls on the Advanced page, stored per endpoint so Bass Morph travels between them. Stiffness bends the upper harmonics sharp of the harmonic series, as a stiff string or a metal bar does, for a metallic, bell-edged bass; the fundamental stays exact, so the Anchor stays locked to it, and higher notes are stiffer, as on a piano. Phase turns every harmonic above the fundamental by up to a quarter cycle: the clean spectrum stays the same, but the wave grows peakier (up to about 6 dB more crest factor), so Harmonic Fold and Character bite harder. A Phase change on a held note glides over at most 100 ms with no click. At 0, both leave the sound exactly as before. Two new factory presets show them off: Stiff Wire and Phase Bite.
- **Registered across the repository** — CI build and test lanes, release packaging and installers, nightly valgrind, clang-tidy, the CPU, shard and close-lane runners, the changelog and specs-index tools, and the root documentation all know about Profundum.
- **73 factory presets in seven categories** — Sub (12), Resonant (8), Harmonic (10), Driven (15), Plucked (8), Animated (9) and Kicks (11); five store POLY with 4 voices for chords. The Kicks are one-hit drums that decay to silence, each with a pitch drop onto the played note: two 808 booms (a tuned one and a deep, clean one), a punch kick, a club kick, a folded kick, a long sub boom, a tight techno kick, a rebound kick, a gabber kick, a hardstyle kick and a lo-fi kick. Each preset leads with one lever of the engine and was authored against a measurement: a render of the preset as stored against the same preset with that lever switched off, so a preset that claims a feature makes it audible. Every preset is checked for mono compatibility, for staying under the output ceiling at full Mass, and for a level within 4 dB of the library median. The presets are generated from the plugin's own parameter surface and installed with the plugin. Every preset is designed on both endpoints: A uses the whole instrument around its lead lever (all six Character algorithms, Harmonic Fold, every Anchor waveform, the three image modes, pitch drop), and Bass Morph travels to a second designed sound at B that sits within 3 dB of A's level, so sweeping Morph changes the sound, not the volume.
- **Preset browser** — A PRESETS button in the header opens the preset browser, with an All tab, one tab per category and its own save dialog. Loading a preset restores the whole saved sound, both endpoints, the endpoint names and the random seed included, also while a note is held. The selected preset's description is shown under the list.
- **User manual** — `MANUAL.md`, with an HTML page under `docs/`, covers the signal flow, every control by its on-screen name, the Anchor / Mass split, Bass Morph with Edit Target and Compare, the Personality macros, and the factory library by category with a one-line description of each preset.
- **Hover help on every control** — Each control's tooltip says how to use it: its range or options and what you will hear. The stereo-field controls also state, in plain words, that the sub stays centred and mono-safe.
- **Signal flow diagram** — The documentation site has a diagram of the whole instrument: the control layer, the per-voice chain with the Anchor on its own path, and the global chain to the output.
- **Version in the editor** — The plugin version is shown under the PROFUNDUM title in the header.
- **Update check** — When the editor opens, Profundum checks online for a newer version, at most once a day, and shows a banner across the top of the window when one exists. A Check for Updates button in the Settings tab checks right away.

### Known limitations

- Host sample rates outside 22050 Hz - 192 kHz are refused; the plugin stays silent at such a rate.
- Velocity is not read.
- In a Linux host that offers no run loop (so the SDK timer cannot run), a value the host changes without the controller seeing it shows on the parameter display only at the next Edit Target switch, state save / load or (de)activation. Hosts that provide the run loop refresh it as on the other systems. The sound and the saved state are always current.
